# Guides' relative .md links resolve outside the SPA, so 92 portal-served links are unreachable

## Context

`learn/**/*.md` has **two consumers**, and a link that is correct for one is broken for the other:

| consumer | what a link must be |
|---|---|
| GitHub reader | a filesystem-relative path that resolves in the repo |
| portal learn section | `#/learn/<id>` where `<id>` is in `learn/tree.json` |

`Portal.view.learn.MainContainerController` resolves a page with `store.get(itemId)` — an **exact** id lookup against `learn/tree.json`, no normalization. **112 of 137 `learn/**/*.md` files are served by the portal.** A relative `.md` href inside one of them is rendered verbatim by `marked` and then resolved by the browser against the *document* URL, which lands outside the app.

Measured in a running portal (`neo-dev-server`), not inferred:

```
learn/agentos/NeuralLink.md
  ./tooling/NeuralLinkCapabilityMatrix.md  -> /apps/portal/tooling/NeuralLinkCapabilityMatrix.md   404
  ../benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md      -> /apps/benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md               404
```

The second one escapes the app directory entirely.

## The count

A corpus sweep over the 112 portal-served guides, extracting links with `marked` (the renderer's own parser) and classifying against `learn/tree.json`:

```
92 unreachable link(s) across 112 portal-served guide(s)
```

Dominated by relative `.md` paths. Two smaller classes ride along: `#/learn/<dotted-id>` links that miss `store.get` (dotted ids do not exist — **0 of 133** `tree.json` ids contain a dot), and bare dotted tokens that are not routes at all.

## Why the fix is the renderer, not the corpus

**Rewriting ~78 relative links to `#/learn/…` would fix the portal and break GitHub.** The link is genuinely correct as authored; what is missing is the portal's translation of it. `N` sites sharing one broken idiom is evidence about the engine, not `N` content defects.

The renderer already owns this seam. `Neo.component.Markdown#render` runs `marked.parse`, then `wrapMarkdownTables`, then an img-wrapping pass — a post-parse HTML rewrite chain that a link rewrite joins naturally. Rewriting the parser's **output** also keeps `marked` the authority on what a link is; rewriting the markdown would re-implement link parsing, which is the exact mistake that produced this ticket.

**Layering, per #12209:** the generic `src/` content class must not bake in a portal route. `issuesUrl` was moved out for precisely this reason and each portal view declares its own. The route prefix here follows that pattern — a config with a neutral default, declared by `Portal.view.learn.Component`.

## Not in scope

- Links from guides to repository **source** files (`../../../src/…​.mjs`). They are unreachable in the portal too, but no route exists for them; that is a separate decision about whether guides should link to source at all.
- Cross-repo absolute URLs (`https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/dev/…`). Live, out of scope here.
- `Neo.component.Markdown`'s `#N` → `issuesUrl` rewrite, which maps every ticket ref to **one hardcoded repo** and post-split can send a reader to a real ticket in the wrong repository. Real, separate, and worse than a dead link because it does not announce itself.

## Contract Ledger

| surface | change | consumer impact |
|---|---|---|
| `Neo.component.Markdown` | new post-parse `rewriteLinks(html)` hook, identity by default | none — existing subclasses inherit a no-op |
| `Neo.app.content.Component` | new `contentRoute_` config, `null` default; resolves relative `.md` hrefs against the current `record.id` | none while unset |
| `Portal.view.learn.Component` | declares `contentRoute: '#/learn/'` | relative `.md` links in served guides become navigable |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A relative `.md` link in a portal-served guide renders as a navigable route, and the **same** link still resolves for a GitHub reader — both surfaces, not a trade
- [ ] The generic `src/` content class carries no portal route; the prefix is declared by the portal view (the #12209 layering holds)
- [ ] `#/learn/<dotted-id>` links and bare dotted tokens are repaired in content — they are navigable on neither surface, so no trade exists
- [ ] The corpus sweep passes with **no allowlist and no exemptions** — an entry-based escape hatch is how the sibling burndown got its 16 entries
- [ ] The sweep is proven able to fail: reverting any single repaired link reddens it
- [ ] Links to repository source files are reported separately, not silently reclassified as acceptable

## Evidence

- Rendered/fetched proof and the full classification: PR #17859 discussion
- Sweep implementation: `test/playwright/unit/app/content/LearnCorpusLinks.spec.mjs`
- Routing-rule arm: `test/playwright/component/component/MarkdownLinkNavigability.spec.mjs`
- Shared predicate: `test/playwright/util/learnLinkNavigability.mjs`

## Residual narrowed — and half of what I wrote about it was wrong

I carried this as *"whether an in-content route link re-renders on click is unproven"*, and on PR #17859 I implied navigation itself might be inert. **Measured in the e2e harness, that half is false.**

```
goto  #/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts   → h1 "Dock Layouts: One Application, Many Windows"
location.hash = '#/learn/benefits/body/Speed'       → h1 "Extreme Speed"
```

**Hash navigation works.** The router, the exact-id `store.get`, the record fetch and the re-render all run, in the harness, within about four seconds. Nothing about routing is broken, and my earlier framing — reached after three contradictory browser observations — should not have been left standing as "may be inert".

**What actually blocks the click arm is the harness, not the app.** `locator.click` on the rewritten anchor exceeds a 90s actionability timeout: Playwright never satisfies its visible/stable/receives-events checks for that element. The same happened to the sidebar tree item, which owes nothing to this feature — which is exactly why I reverted the arm rather than shipping a red whose control was also red.

**So the residual is narrower than stated:**

| | status |
|---|---|
| the rewrite emits a valid route | ✅ proven, mutation-verified (`LearnLinkRoutingNL.spec.mjs`) |
| that route renders the destination | ✅ proven above |
| a **click** on it is actionable in the e2e harness | ❌ open — an element-reachability question |

The remaining gap is *"can Playwright click content inside the portal's scroll container"*, not *"do links work"*. That is worth solving once for this tier — several future portal arms will want it — and it is not something the link rewrite can answer.

I am not filing a ticket for it tonight: the seats that would pick it up are rate-limited or busy, and a ticket nobody can resolve is a rate-limit violation, not a hand-off. It stays here, on the ticket that owns it, with the measurement attached so the next person starts from a narrowed question rather than my earlier wrong one.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code

- 2026-08-30T07:18:26Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `04596be` - "fix(content): the link rewrite must see the quote styles the guard sees (#17877)

The build-time guard extracts raw-HTML anchors with `["']`; `rewriteLinks` matched
only `href="`. Two consumers of one corpus, two different predicates - so a
single-quoted relative link validates as healthy at build time and is then rendered
unrewritten, producing a href that works in a file tree and 404s in the SPA. That is
precisely the failure this pair exists to prevent, and it would be invisible.

Not hypothetical authoring: the corpus already carries two single-quoted anchors
(learn/guides/userinteraction/events/DomEvents.md:7 and :25). Both are absolute
https targets, so no link is broken today - the idiom is present, the relative case
has simply not been written yet.

The rewrite now mirrors HTML_HREF exactly and preserves the original quote
character, since normalising the delimiter would corrupt any attribute following it
on the same tag.

The corpus sweep's own oracle carried the same double-quote-only pattern, so it
would have skipped single-quoted anchors while reporting the population clean - a
third copy of the diverging predicate, in the instrument meant to detect it. Fixed,
and its capture group moved from 1 to 2 now that group 1 is the quote.

The sweep can only fail on links that exist today, so it cannot witness a quote
style the corpus has not yet used for a relative target. An explicit arm covers
both styles; reverting the regex to double-quote-only reds it."
- 2026-08-30T07:40:13Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `6690355` - "fix(links): guard and renderer share one predicate, and the portal fossil is gone (#17877)

Two divergences between the build-time guard and the runtime rewriter, both of which
certified something the other could not honour. They ship together because they are
one contract.

SCHEME AND CASE. URI schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 3986 3.1) and both readers
honour that, but both sides tested case-sensitively - and failed in OPPOSITE
directions on the same href. Given `HTTPS://example.com/docs/Foo.md`, rewriteLinks
did not skip it and rewrote a live absolute URL into `#/learn/...`, while the guard
classified it as a repository path and reported a live URL as a dead link.
`MailTo:a@b.c` classified as a portal ref. Both sides are now case-insensitive and
match ANY scheme rather than an enumerated list, which is what an absolute URI is.
The guard exports EXTERNAL_TARGET so the pair is pinned in one table; `src/` must not
import `buildScripts/`, so the duplication stays, but it is auditable now instead of
silent. `.md` is matched case-insensitively too.

Root-absolute is the one deliberate divergence and has its own arm: the renderer
leaves it alone (correct for a file-tree reader) while the guard REPORTS it, since
neither reader resolves a leading slash against the repository.

THE PORTAL FOSSIL. The guard resolved a portal ref by `id.replaceAll('.', '/') +
'.md'` and checking for that file. That rule described addressing the portal had
already left: 0 of 135 live tree.json ids contain a dot. So the guard certified
`benefits.body.ConfigSystem` as HEALTHY - a form dead in both readers, since the
router does an exact `store.get(itemId)` and no such file exists to open either. It
passed only by resolving onto a file a differently-spelled id owns. A guard that
blesses a known-dead syntax is fail-open for every future edit, which is the one
thing this guard exists not to be.

Portal refs are now judged by tree.json membership, which is the router's actual
predicate. That also fixes the other direction: `Benefits` and `GettingStarted` are
live ids for section nodes with NO markdown file, and any path-based rule reports
them dead. Restoring the dot-to-slash rule reds three arms, one per direction plus
the corpus arm.

A documented limit is pinned rather than left implied: live ids are slash-separated,
and a slash-separated target cannot be told from a relative path, so only the
slash-less form is ever classified `portal`.

The first version of the parity spec duplicated the renderer's regex as a local
helper and compared two literals both written in the test. It passed with the
production regex reverted to the buggy form, because it never touched production
code - the same mistake this PR was already corrected for once. It now drives the
real `rewriteLinks`; reverting the predicate reds 5 arms, each naming its href class."

Custody decisions move link targets; nothing moves the referrers, and until now nothing
could see the difference. `grep -rlE "link.?check|markdown.?link|dead.?link"` over
`.github/workflows/` and `buildScripts/` returned nothing.

THE TICKET'S OWN PREMISE DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and that is in the ticket's comments rather
than fixed here: `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` resolves 0 dead links at every ref
including the one it names. The cut commit repointed those 8 links to absolute Brain URLs in
the same commit that removed the trees. What the sweep DID find is a different population,
and a better argument for the guard — these are relative-depth mistakes, not split fallout,
so ordinary authoring is the hazard and no custody decision would have prevented them.

    learn/benefits/body/JSONFirstUIs.md              ../guides/…      -> ../../guides/…
    learn/benefits/body/ObjectPermanence.md          ../guides/…      -> ../../guides/…
    learn/benefits/body/Speed.md                     ../../examples/… -> ../../../examples/…
    learn/blog/the-organism-already-existed.md       learn/guides/…   -> ../guides/…   (x2)
    learn/blog/v10-deep-dive-vdom-revolution.md      .github/RELEASE_NOTES/v10.3.0.md
                                                     -> resources/content/release-notes/chunk-2/v10.3.0.md
    learn/guides/fundamentals/ApplicationBootstrap.md ../benefits/…   -> ../../benefits/…
    learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/HtmlTemplates…      buildScripts/buildESModules.mjs
                                                     -> buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs

Every repoint target verified present in the tracked tree first: a link that 404s somewhere
new is not an improvement. Two needed real answers rather than a depth fix — the release
notes moved to `resources/content/release-notes/` (no `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/` tree exists,
and `v10.3.0` has no GitHub release either, so a canonical URL would have 404'd too), and
the build script was renamed to `build/esmodules.mjs`, confirmed by finding the same
`processFileContent` import the prose describes. Its link TEXT named the old path, so both
moved.

The guard resolves against `git ls-files` — the index — not the filesystem. That is the
whole point: a checkout still carrying trees a merge removed reports every link healthy,
because the targets are sitting right there untracked. The index also includes staged
additions, so a PR may add a guide and link to it in one commit.

Three link classes, because two are not paths. A first pass over this repository produced 17
findings of which 7 were real: six were root-absolute links joined to the referrer's
directory instead of the repo root, and three were the portal's dotted addressing
(`guides.events.DomEvents`), which is not a filesystem path at all. Both are handled, and
skipped portal refs are counted in the output rather than silently dropped.

It reads reference-style and HTML links as well as inline ones, which is how the 8th finding
surfaced — `Speed.md`'s dead `<a href>` is invisible to an inline-only parser, and "no
findings" from a partial parser is indistinguishable from "no problems".

Wired into lint-staged on `learn/**/*.md` and a CI workflow triggered by `learn/**` plus the
guard's own files, so a checker that stops working is caught by the trigger that would have
caught the links.

Round-1 RA-1 from @neo-gpt: the exemption should be positive portal authority, not a suffix

link fix: the file had never been staged, so `check-whitespace` had never seen it, and it

Root-absolute targets no longer resolve from the repository root. Both readers
resolve them against an ORIGIN - a browser on GitHub sends /learn/x.md to
github.com/learn/x.md, and the portal sends it outside the app - so treating the
leading slash as "repo root" reported dead links as healthy. The first pass
over-corrected in the opposite direction, inventing six false positives by
joining them to the referrer; the honest answer is that there is no repository
path to check. Tightening it immediately surfaced a seventh live instance in
learn/blog that six manual repairs had missed.

learn/ now requires the unit suite. It is docs-only by path but not by
consequence: its links are checked against learn/tree.json, so a guide-only edit
can introduce a route resolving to no record, and the corpus gate was skipped on
exactly the PRs it exists to catch.

The check-whitespace --fix flag is reverted. It belongs to neither close target,
and it silently deleted a real Markdown hard break: Earthquakes.md:127 ends a
line whose successor is a continuation, so the two trailing spaces render a
line break. That break is restored explicitly as <br>, which survives a lint
that cannot tell semantics from accident.

* test(portal): an e2e arm that catches deleting the link rewrite (#17877)

The component and corpus arms proved properties of the rewrite in isolation, and
both stayed green when the production rewriteLinks invocation was deleted, because
neither executed it. Mutating the predicate is not mutating the feature.

This arm drives the real Portal, so the render path, the view's declared route,
the router and the tree store all participate. Both named mutations now red it:
removing the hook call, and removing the Portal's contentRoute.

A click arm was written and reverted. Its control - clicking the sidebar tree,
which owes nothing to this feature - failed in the same harness, and a red
assertion whose control is also red measures the harness rather than the subject.
Whether an in-content route link re-renders on click is therefore still open, and
is recorded as open rather than asserted either way.

* fix(test): the corpus sweep skipped every top-level learn guide (#17877)

git ls-files 'learn/**/*.md' does not match learn/*.md, so two served guides sat
outside the population while the run still reported clean. Surfaced by a reviewer
citing 114/137 nested against 116/140 including top-level: the count was not just
stale, the gap between the two numbers was the sweep's blind spot.

* fix(content): the link rewrite must see the quote styles the guard sees (#17877)

The build-time guard extracts raw-HTML anchors with `["']`; `rewriteLinks` matched
only `href="`. Two consumers of one corpus, two different predicates - so a
single-quoted relative link validates as healthy at build time and is then rendered
unrewritten, producing a href that works in a file tree and 404s in the SPA. That is
precisely the failure this pair exists to prevent, and it would be invisible.

Not hypothetical authoring: the corpus already carries two single-quoted anchors
(learn/guides/userinteraction/events/DomEvents.md:7 and :25). Both are absolute
https targets, so no link is broken today - the idiom is present, the relative case
has simply not been written yet.

The rewrite now mirrors HTML_HREF exactly and preserves the original quote
character, since normalising the delimiter would corrupt any attribute following it
on the same tag.

The corpus sweep's own oracle carried the same double-quote-only pattern, so it
would have skipped single-quoted anchors while reporting the population clean - a
third copy of the diverging predicate, in the instrument meant to detect it. Fixed,
and its capture group moved from 1 to 2 now that group 1 is the quote.

The sweep can only fail on links that exist today, so it cannot witness a quote
style the corpus has not yet used for a relative target. An explicit arm covers
both styles; reverting the regex to double-quote-only reds it.

* test(build): the guard's index-authority claim is witnessed, not asserted (#17809)

Every existing arm injects `tracked` and `read`, which proves the resolver and
nothing about where the CLI's inputs come from. The module header's central claim -
membership is the git index, so staged edits are scanned and a stale checkout's
untracked leftovers stay invisible - had no test at all. That claim is the entire
reason the guard resolves against git rather than the filesystem, and it was the one
thing not covered.

`trackedFiles` and the staged reader are now exported with an injectable root, so a
real repository can witness them. The reader is named `stagedReader` because what it
does is read `:path`, not open a file.

The new arms build a throwaway repo with a committed file, a staged-but-uncommitted
file, and an untracked file on disk, then edit the staged file in the working tree
so index and worktree DIFFER. Without that divergence both readers return the same
bytes and the arm cannot tell them apart - it would pass against a filesystem
implementation. Pointing the reader at the worktree, or membership at `ls`, reds
them.

Also adds the single-quoted raw-HTML control the suite lacked. The guard already
handled both quote styles; nothing proved it, and the runtime rewriter had silently
diverged to double-quote-only (fixed in the preceding commit). Narrowing HTML_HREF
back to `"` reds the new arm.

* fix(links): guard and renderer share one predicate, and the portal fossil is gone (#17877)

Two divergences between the build-time guard and the runtime rewriter, both of which
certified something the other could not honour. They ship together because they are
one contract.

SCHEME AND CASE. URI schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 3986 3.1) and both readers
honour that, but both sides tested case-sensitively - and failed in OPPOSITE
directions on the same href. Given `HTTPS://example.com/docs/Foo.md`, rewriteLinks
did not skip it and rewrote a live absolute URL into `#/learn/...`, while the guard
classified it as a repository path and reported a live URL as a dead link.
`MailTo:a@b.c` classified as a portal ref. Both sides are now case-insensitive and
match ANY scheme rather than an enumerated list, which is what an absolute URI is.
The guard exports EXTERNAL_TARGET so the pair is pinned in one table; `src/` must not
import `buildScripts/`, so the duplication stays, but it is auditable now instead of
silent. `.md` is matched case-insensitively too.

Root-absolute is the one deliberate divergence and has its own arm: the renderer
leaves it alone (correct for a file-tree reader) while the guard REPORTS it, since
neither reader resolves a leading slash against the repository.

THE PORTAL FOSSIL. The guard resolved a portal ref by `id.replaceAll('.', '/') +
'.md'` and checking for that file. That rule described addressing the portal had
already left: 0 of 135 live tree.json ids contain a dot. So the guard certified
`benefits.body.ConfigSystem` as HEALTHY - a form dead in both readers, since the
router does an exact `store.get(itemId)` and no such file exists to open either. It
passed only by resolving onto a file a differently-spelled id owns. A guard that
blesses a known-dead syntax is fail-open for every future edit, which is the one
thing this guard exists not to be.

Portal refs are now judged by tree.json membership, which is the router's actual
predicate. That also fixes the other direction: `Benefits` and `GettingStarted` are
live ids for section nodes with NO markdown file, and any path-based rule reports
them dead. Restoring the dot-to-slash rule reds three arms, one per direction plus
the corpus arm.

A documented limit is pinned rather than left implied: live ids are slash-separated,
and a slash-separated target cannot be told from a relative path, so only the
slash-less form is ever classified `portal`.

The first version of the parity spec duplicated the renderer's regex as a local
helper and compared two literals both written in the test. It passed with the
production regex reverted to the buggy form, because it never touched production
code - the same mistake this PR was already corrected for once. It now drives the
real `rewriteLinks`; reverting the predicate reds 5 arms, each naming its href class.

* fix(build): the classifier was case-blind on suffixes, and the remedy text taught the fossil (#17809)

Two remnants of the same two clauses, both found by a reviewer reading the code
rather than the diff.

SUFFIX CASE. `FILE_SUFFIXES.some(value.endsWith)` was case-sensitive, so `Foo.MD`
classified as `portal` rather than `path` — a markdown file then judged against
tree.json membership and reported dead. Same class as the scheme fix in the previous
commit and it should have shipped with it: `Foo.MD` is one file on every system this
corpus is read on.

My own arm could not have caught it. It used `./Splitters.MD`, whose SLASH reaches
the path branch on `includes('/')` before the suffix test ever runs - it looks like a
case arm while witnessing nothing. The extension branch is only reachable for a bare
filename, so the new arms carry no slash.

REMEDY TEXT. Portal findings are unresolved by construction now, so the CLI's
`resolved === null` test described every dead dotted id as "is root-absolute", and
the footer instructed `learn/<dots-become-slashes>.md` - prescribing the exact rule
the previous commit retired. A dotted-id failure correctly reds, then tells the
author to restore the fossil that caused it.

Description now branches on KIND, and the footer states the real contract: ids match
learn/tree.json exactly, and relative .md links are rewritten for you. Extracted as
`describeFinding` so the prose is pinned by a spec instead of being reachable only by
running the binary - the guard's stated authority is part of what it must get right,
which is the whole reason this ticket exists.

Both mutants red only their own arm: case-sensitive suffix test reds the extension
arm, and collapsing the portal branch reds the remedy arm."
